rationale: No displayed candidate contains the child’s distinctive machinery: creation of a Chief-of-Mission-level High Commissioner, concentration of nonmilitary United States governmental functions in Germany, a defined relationship with the military commander, resolution of civil-military policy disputes, emergency military authority, and a transitional period in which the High Commissioner also serves as Military Governor. C10 has the nearest abstract resemblance in assigning supervision through a defense hierarchy, C11 allocates responsibilities among officials and provides consultation rules, and C13 transfers functions on a transitional timetable, but these are isolated and generic administrative similarities rather than a concrete, material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The High Commissioner shall have the authority, under the immediate supervision of the Secretary of State ... to exercise all of the governmental function of the United States in Germany
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Secretary of Defense is authorized and directed to supervise and control, on behalf of the President and through such official or officials ... as the said Secretary shall designate
shared_material.explanation: C10 shares hierarchical supervision-and-control language, but its subject, allocation of authority, and operative structure are materially different.

shared_material.child_excerpt: If major differences arise over policy affecting military matters, necessary reports and recommendations shall be referred to the Department of State and to the national Military Establishment for resolution.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Director's determination ... shall be made after consulting appropriate Federal executive agencies and giving due consideration to any responsibility now exercised by any of them
shared_material.explanation: C11 likewise coordinates authority among agencies, but this is a general administrative mechanism and does not reproduce the child’s civil-military command relationship.

shared_material.child_excerpt: In the event that the High Commissioner shall assume his duties ... prior to the date that the Military Government ... is terminated, he shall during such interval ... be the United States Military Governor
shared_material.parent_excerpt: such transfer to become effective as to any particular cemetery or group of cemeteries upon the completion of the operational mission of the Department of the Army ... but in no instance later than December 31, 1951
shared_material.explanation: C13 contains a transition keyed to completion of an Army mission, but it concerns transfer of cemetery administration and supplies no substantial language or machinery for the child’s office-and-command arrangement.
